root_cause.text: The ASoC SDCA interrupt setup used `devm_request_threaded_irq()` from component probe, so IRQ handlers were tied to the device-managed lifetime and could remain active after the sound card/component was torn down, letting callbacks run with freed card/kcontrol references.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says IRQs “can persist if the sound card is torn down” and handlers “store references to the card and the kcontrols which can then fail”; the patch fixes this by replacing `devm_request_threaded_irq()` with `request_threaded_irq()` and adding explicit `sdca_irq_cleanup()`/`sdca_irq_free()` in the component `.remove` path to manually free the IRQs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a corresponding SDCA IRQ free API to support releasing interrupt resources.
intent_record.what: A new function prototype, `sdca_irq_free(...)`, was added to the `sdca` interrupt API declaration alongside the existing `sdca_irq_request(...)` prototype.
intent_record.how: This change exposes a cleanup/release interface for SDCA IRQ resources, allowing callers to explicitly free an IRQ previously requested through this subsystem.

intent_record.intent_summary: Declare the SDCA IRQ cleanup helper so interrupt setup can be properly torn down when needed.
intent_record.what: A new function prototype, `sdca_irq_cleanup(struct sdca_function_data *function, struct snd_soc_component *component, struct sdca_interrupt_info *info);`, was added to the header between the existing `sdca_irq_populate` declaration and the `sdca_irq_allocate` declaration.
intent_record.how: This makes the cleanup routine available to other translation units, allowing code that sets up SDCA IRQ handling to explicitly tear it down later. At runtime, it enables proper resource release and interrupt-related state cleanup when SDCA IRQ setup needs to be undone.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add component removal cleanup to release SDCA IRQ resources when the ASoC component is removed.
intent_record.what: A new static function `class_function_component_remove()` was added. It retrieves the driver data and core driver pointer from the ASoC component, then calls `sdca_irq_cleanup(drv->function, component, core->irq_info);` during component removal.
intent_record.how: This adds explicit cleanup logic when the sound component is removed, ensuring IRQ-related resources or state populated during probe are torn down properly and avoiding stale IRQ setup after the component is unloaded.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the component remove callback so the driver performs proper cleanup on detach.
intent_record.what: A .remove callback was added to the static snd_soc_component_driver initializer for class_function_component_drv, pointing to class_function_component_remove.
intent_record.how: When the component is unloaded or detached, the driver will now invoke the remove handler, allowing any cleanup logic in class_function_component_remove to run instead of leaving teardown unhandled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch the IRQ request from device-managed to manual registration while preserving the same threaded interrupt handler setup.
intent_record.what: The call inside sdca_irq_request_locked() was changed from devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, handler, IRQF_ONESHOT, name, data) to request_threaded_irq(irq, NULL, handler, IRQF_ONESHOT, name, data).
intent_record.how: The IRQ is now registered without device-managed lifetime tracking, so it will no longer be automatically freed when the device is detached; instead, the caller must manage IRQ teardown explicitly. The runtime interrupt handling behavior otherwise remains the same.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to properly free an SDCA IRQ and clear its tracked state.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function `sdca_irq_free_locked()` was added. It takes a device, interrupt info, SDCA IRQ index, name, and data pointer, looks up the Linux virtual IRQ with `regmap_irq_get_virq()`, returns early if the lookup fails, otherwise calls `free_irq()` on that IRQ, clears `info->irqs[sdca_irq].irq` to 0, and logs a debug message.
intent_record.how: This enables the driver to explicitly release a previously requested IRQ and reset its tracked state, preventing stale IRQ bookkeeping and ensuring the handler is detached when the interrupt is no longer needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a public helper to safely free one SDCA interrupt early so cleanup can skip it and avoid duplicate teardown.
intent_record.what: A new exported function `sdca_irq_free()` was added. It takes `dev`, `info`, `sdca_irq`, `name`, and `data`, checks that `sdca_irq` is within `[0, SDCA_MAX_INTERRUPTS)`, acquires `info->irq_lock` with `guard(mutex)`, and then calls `sdca_irq_free_locked(dev, info, sdca_irq, name, data)`. The function is documented as a way to manually free an individual SDCA interrupt before `sdca_irq_cleanup()`. It is exported with `EXPORT_SYMBOL_NS_GPL` in the `SND_SOC_SDCA` namespace.
intent_record.how: This enables callers to explicitly release a single SDCA IRQ entry instead of relying solely on the full cleanup path. By freeing one interrupt early, custom IRQ users can mark it as already handled so later cleanup skips it, preventing double-free or redundant teardown of that IRQ while leaving other interrupts intact.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch `name` allocation in `sdca_irq_data_populate()` from device-managed to manual allocation.
intent_record.what: In sdca_irq_data_populate(), the allocation of the formatted string variable `name` was changed from `devm_kasprintf(dev, GFP_KERNEL, "%s %s %s", function->desc->name, entity->label, control->label)` to `kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "%s %s %s", function->desc->name, entity->label, control->label)`, while keeping the existing `if (!name) return -ENOMEM;` check unchanged.
intent_record.how: The string is no longer tied to the device-managed lifetime mechanism and is now allocated as a plain heap string. At runtime this changes ownership semantics: the caller must ensure the returned buffer is freed appropriately elsewhere, otherwise it can leak, but it also avoids devres-managed cleanup for this allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an SDCA IRQ cleanup helper to safely free all IRQs and names belonging to a function during teardown.
intent_record.what: A new exported function `sdca_irq_cleanup()` was added. It takes an SDCA function, ASoC component, and interrupt info, locks `info->irq_lock`, iterates over all `SDCA_MAX_INTERRUPTS` entries, selects entries whose `interrupt->function` matches the given function and whose `irq` is non-zero, calls `sdca_irq_free_locked(dev, info, i, interrupt->name, interrupt)`, and then frees `interrupt->name` with `kfree()`. The function is also documented with a kernel-doc comment and exported via `EXPORT_SYMBOL_NS_GPL`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this provides a cleanup path that releases all IRQ resources associated with a specific SDCA function and frees their associated name strings, preventing those IRQ entries from remaining allocated after the function is torn down. The lock ensures the cleanup is performed safely against concurrent IRQ table access.

The changes directly address the reported bug by adding explicit SDCA IRQ teardown and component remove cleanup, preventing IRQ handlers from persisting after the sound card/component is torn down and avoiding callbacks on freed objects.

candidates.rationale: This device-managed IRQ request ties the threaded handler lifetime to the component/device probe path instead of the card/component teardown path, so the IRQ can still fire after the sound card or kcontrol data has been freed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This device-managed IRQ request ties the threaded handler lifetime to the component/device probe path instead of the card/component teardown path, allowing the IRQ handler to remain active after the sound card or related kcontrol data has been freed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present here. This code uses the regmap IRQ framework via `devm_regmap_add_irq_chip()` in `sdca_irq_allocate()` rather than directly installing per-IRQ handlers from component probe. The only request path shown is `sdca_irq_request_locked()`, which calls `devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, handler, IRQF_ONESHOT, name, data);` on a regmap-generated VIRQ. In addition, the IRQ data is stored in `sdca_interrupt_info` and protected by a mutex, and the library explicitly allocates the IRQ chip with `devm_regmap_add_irq_chip()` instead of tying ad-hoc handlers to the component lifetime. There is no evidence in this snippet of the old unsafe pattern where IRQ handlers outlive card teardown and callback into freed card/kcontrol state. Since the described bug is absent and the code already uses the safer managed regmap-IRQ setup, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
